method: Same mission, route (3 spots, 30 s moves), 20 minutes and three death/restart cycles. Control: every co-op system off (bridge transport/status only), both peers die together and restart natively. Slope = least-squares private-memory MB/min after the 2-minute baseline; within-segment rate excludes the restart steps and the first minute after each restart (transient load peak).
findings: Confirmed runtime: with every co-op system off (bridge transport/status writers only) private memory still grows ~5 MB/min at steady state on both peers (host 4.92, client 5.25) plus ~187 MB across three native restarts.
With the product controller (1186) the steady rate is 5.97/7.14 MB/min: the co-op systems add at most ~1-2 MB/min over the control; most growth is present without them.
Handles stayed flat in both runs; no crash; transport fresh throughout.
outstanding: Vanilla baseline without the proxy DLL (requires relaunching a lab instance without dinput8) to separate the game from the always-on bridge.
Longer (2 h) soak to see whether growth plateaus (native streaming caches) or continues.
